data.title: Where Polanyi Meets Galois: Tacit Knowing as an Algebro-Deterministic Operation, Toward Re-rooting AI-Generated Science
data.description: arXiv:2610.16102v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Tacit knowing is an operating regime of one memory substrate, not a separate kind of content. In VaCoAl (CASRAM, PyVaCoAl), an algebro-deterministic hyperdimensional memory over GF(2), one DAG of bound records is read in two ways. With every collision repaired (Rescue), the trace is exactly auditable but no path outranks another; with collisions tolerated (Don't Care), a path-integrated confidence $CR_2$ ranks direct over circuitous routes without being stated. This audit-valuation complementarity formalizes Polanyi's claim that tacit and explicit knowledge are not sharply divided. (1) Polanyi's from-to structure reads as non-commutative binding. (2) Full explication destroys the valuation (Lemma 1), as with Polanyi's pianist; tacitness is contingent or regime-bound, placing Polanyi, Nonaka, Tsoukas and Collins on one substrate. (3) The same lemma answers the popular dual-process moral ("train slow System 2 to tame fast System 1"), which mirrors the two-store reading of knowledge Polanyi rejected; Mercier and Sperber's reply, that reasoning is intuitive inference about reasons, matches his. (4) To know a large DAG is to cull it. Simon answered Polanyi's Meno argument: a test and a generator suffice. The AlphaGo-to-AlphaProof lineage builds that answer, yet a checker audits an endpoint and values no path: the tacit is relocated, not removed, and results are verified yet rootless. (5) Collins's three tacit knowledges map to bound structure, substrate valuation and value binding. (6) Our mentor-student DAG charts tacit transmission. (7) AI-solved problems with few follow-ups (Tao) are rootless explicit knowledge, re-rooted when LLMs generate, VaCoAl keeps the trace and the community values. (8) On Mercier and Sperber's theory an LLM is a sophist; truth-seeking lies in collective tacit knowing, Polanyi's conviviality, which we conjecture extends beyond humans. Testable predictions follow.
data.author: Hiroyuki Chuma, Kanji Otsuka, Yoichi Sato, Kodo Yamauchi
